estrutura.personaBrief: Rosa Luxemburg rejected federalism and national self-determination as bourgeois ideas, and the Spartacist programme called for abolishing the German states in favour of a unitary socialist republic; at the same time she defended democratic local self-government and initiative from below.

representacao.personaBrief: She advocated a dictatorship of the proletariat understood as mass democracy, with elections, a free press and freedom 'for the one who thinks differently', and criticized Lenin for dissolving the Constituent Assembly; even so, she preferred workers' council power to bourgeois parliamentarism.

poder.personaBrief: Imprisoned several times for anti-war agitation and persecuted by the state, she defended a free press, the right of assembly and the abolition of the death penalty, and wanted to arm the workers rather than strengthen the police.

imigracao.personaBrief: A Polish Jew living in Germany and a radical internationalist, she saw nationalism as a bourgeois ideology, fought the forced Germanization of Poles and championed workers' solidarity across borders.

diplomacia.personaBrief: She fought militarism and the First World War as products of imperialism and wanted to replace the standing army with a people's militia, but she also distrusted bourgeois utopias of disarmament and arbitration.

intervencao.personaBrief: In the Junius Pamphlet she rejected the 'national interest' and great-power politics as masks for imperialism and argued for proletarian neutrality in wars, but her revolutionary internationalism also refused national isolationism.

economia.personaBrief: She called for socializing the means of production under workers' council control and expropriating large holdings, including land, which should become socialist cooperatives, and saw reformism as insufficient given the need for revolution.

controle.personaBrief: As a Marxist she wanted to replace the anarchy of the market with a planned socialist economy coordinated collectively by the workers, but she rejected state support for national capitalists and cartels.

comercio.personaBrief: She fought the Junkers' agrarian tariffs and cartelized protectionism for making workers' bread more expensive and feeding militarism, and saw the world economy as a single whole; at the same time she denounced imperialist capital export and the dependency it created.

religiao.personaBrief: An atheist of secular Jewish background, she saw the institutional Church as an ally of the oppressors (Socialism and the Churches, 1905) and wanted to separate Church and state, but treated faith as a private matter of individual conscience.

moral.personaBrief: A revolutionary who lived unconventionally and championed women's suffrage and emancipation, she rejected the bourgeois family and traditional morality as pillars of the class order, and saw prostitution as a product of capitalist exploitation.

tecnologia.personaBrief: A Marxist who saw industrial development as the material basis of socialism, she was also an amateur botanist who lamented the disappearance of birds caused by modern agriculture and denounced the colonial destruction of non-capitalist peoples and lands.
